note: Ghana's large banks were tried for credit card terms: Absa Bank Ghana, Stanbic Bank Ghana, Zenith Bank Ghana, Access Bank Ghana, UBA Ghana and Standard Chartered Ghana, chosen as the best-known card issuers (the Bank of Ghana's rankings weren't needed, as only Absa publishes current card terms that could be read). Absa Bank Ghana's tariff guide (September 2026), read in full: its Classic and Platinum credit cards cost GHS 100 and GHS 150 a year, bear 43% and 40% a year, charge 5% for a cash advance, a 7% scheme mark-up on spending abroad, a minimum monthly repayment of 5%, and give up to 55 days interest free. The late payment fee (10% or GHS 20, whichever is higher) doesn't say 10% of what, so it isn't written. The guide's Signature and Infinite credit cards carry fees (GHS 170 and GHS 200 a year, a GHS 200 issue fee on the Infinite, GHS 25 late, 5% cash advance) but no interest rate, so they can't be written. Stanbic Ghana's credit card page refused this client (403); Zenith Ghana's 2025 tariff guides answered 404; Access Bank Ghana's tariff guide is served with an expired certificate and wasn't fetched; UBA Ghana's 2026 tariff guide prices no credit card rate; Standard Chartered's Ghana tariff guide dates from January 2018 and isn't current. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a second and third bank: Republic Bank (Ghana) was added, the next card issuer whose site links a current tariff guide with its cards' rate. Its Tariff Guide (current update March 2026), read in full for its Visa credit cards: the Classic, Adeshie (its private banking card; that condition isn't checked) and Infinite cards cost GHS 100, 100 and 200 to issue and GHS 150, 150 and 400 a year, charge 3.75% a month on the outstanding balance, 3% of a cash advance plus GHS 15 (the guide's '3% of amount + GHS 15.00/Min GHS 15.00' is read as both, the GHS 15 being the least it costs), 5.5% on spending across the border, a late payment fee of 10% of the overdue amount or GHS 50, whichever is higher (the overdue amount written as the unpaid part), and 5% of the amount over the limit, at least GHS 100 per billing cycle. The Business card isn't written; the 2% 'Visa optional issuer fee' doesn't say what it is charged on and isn't written. GCB Bank's 2026 tariff guide and Fidelity Bank Ghana's (August 2026) were read and price no credit card; Stanbic Ghana's and Ecobank Ghana's sites answered a captcha, Consolidated Bank Ghana's an Incapsula check, and Standard Chartered Ghana's credit card pages answered 404, its latest tariff guide being from 2018. So Ghana has two banks' cards. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: No minimum payment is published for Republic Bank (Ghana)'s Classic, Adeshie and Infinite cards; tried: the three card pages (read 2026-10-30: eligibility, limits and benefits, no repayment share), its March 2026 tariff guide (none), and archive.org's API (a snapshot of the Classic page of 10 May 2026; web.archive.org itself is refused by this research's connection); the Bank of Ghana's rules weren't searched for want of the budget.
